"""Extend the hash-matched page evidence with five bounded operator probes."""
import hashlib
import json
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import time

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PRIOR = ROOT / 'target/arm64-recognition-sme-final-20261017'
assert not (OUT / 'operators.json').exists(), 'Do not overwrite or rerun samples'
sha = lambda p: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
comparison = json.loads((PRIOR / 'page-comparison.json').read_text())
profiles = json.loads((PRIOR / 'profiles.json').read_text())
sources = lambda: {str(p.relative_to(ROOT)): sha(p) for p in sorted((ROOT / 'src').rglob('*.rs'))}
assert comparison['candidate_source_sha256'] == sources()
assert sha(PRIOR / 'cpu_benchmark') == comparison['binary_sha256']['after']
assert sha(PRIOR / 'cpu_profile') == profiles['binary_sha256']
# The examples, harness and build configuration have not changed since their
# recorded base revision; the production source hashes above match exactly.
subprocess.run(['git', 'diff', '--exit-code', comparison['baseline_head'], 'HEAD', '--',
                'examples', 'tools', 'Cargo.toml', 'Cargo.lock', 'rust-toolchain.toml'],
               cwd=ROOT, check=True, capture_output=True)
manifest = json.loads((ROOT / 'tests/baseline/manifest.json').read_text())
for asset in manifest['assets']:
    assert sha(ROOT.parent / 'SimdPaddleOCR/models' / asset['file']) in [asset['sha256'], asset.get('sha256_crlf')]
log = (OUT / 'correctness-profile.log').read_text()
assert '7 passed; 0 failed' in log
assert '4 passed; 0 failed' in (OUT / 'correctness-sme.log').read_text()
binary = ROOT / re.search(r'Running unittests src/lib.rs \(([^)]+)\)', log)[1]
prior_seconds = profiles['final_version_total_performance_execution_seconds']
used = prior_seconds
commands, diagnostics = [], []
for name in ['sparse_detector_production_steps', 'recognition_backbone_physical_steps']:
    command = [str(binary), 'runtime::optimized::tests::performance::' + name,
               '--exact', '--ignored', '--nocapture', '--test-threads=1']
    started = time.monotonic()
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True,
                            timeout=min(12, 60-used))
    seconds = time.monotonic() - started
    used += seconds
    (OUT / (name + '.log')).write_text(result.stdout + result.stderr)
    commands.append(dict(command=command, elapsed_seconds=seconds))
    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stdout + result.stderr
    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
        match = re.search(r'(small|medium) REC width=(\d+) .*total_step_ms=([\d.]+); groups=(\{.*\})', line)
        if match:
            diagnostics.append(dict(kind='recognition_backbone', model=match[1],
                shape=[1,3,48,int(match[2])], threads=1, input='deterministic synthetic; vocabulary head excluded',
                total_step_ms=float(match[3]), groups_ms=json.loads(match[4]), outputs_exactly_equal=True, top_steps=[]))
        elif re.match(r'[\d.]+ms node=', line):
            ms, description = line.split('ms ', 1)
            diagnostics[-1]['top_steps'].append(dict(ms=float(ms), description=description))
        elif 'detector_production_steps {' in line:
            diagnostics.append(dict(kind='detector', **json.loads(line[line.index('{'):])) )
    print(name, f'{seconds:.3f}s; cumulative current-version performance {used:.3f}s', flush=True)
assert len(diagnostics) == 5
assert comparison['candidate_source_sha256'] == sources()
report = dict(head=subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],cwd=ROOT,text=True).strip(),
    source_matches_existing_page_evidence=True, source_sha256=sources(),
    reused_comparison_sha256=sha(PRIOR/'page-comparison.json'), reused_profiles_sha256=sha(PRIOR/'profiles.json'),
    reused_portable_evidence_sha256=sha(ROOT/'docs/reports/macos-arm64-2026-10-17-sme-optimization.json'),
    test_binary_sha256=sha(binary), manifest_sha256=sha(ROOT/'tests/baseline/manifest.json'),
    machine=subprocess.check_output(['sysctl','-n','machdep.cpu.brand_string','hw.ncpu','hw.memsize'],text=True),
    os=subprocess.check_output(['sw_vers'],text=True),
    rustc=subprocess.check_output(['rustc','-Vv'],cwd=ROOT,text=True),
    power_source=subprocess.check_output(['pmset','-g','batt'],text=True),
    thermal_status=subprocess.check_output(['pmset','-g','therm'],text=True,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT),
    diagnostics=diagnostics, commands=commands, prior_performance_execution_seconds=prior_seconds,
    new_performance_execution_seconds=used-prior_seconds, cumulative_performance_execution_seconds=used,
    counts=dict(new_detector_warmups=3,new_detector_measured_passes=3,new_recognition_warmups=2,new_recognition_measured_passes=2),
    method='No page reruns. Five operator shapes, one warm-up and one fused instrumented pass each; sequential subprocesses; 12-second per-command and remaining aggregate 60-second cap.')
(OUT / 'operators.json').write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2)+'\n')

"""Package existing current-source page samples and new operator evidence."""
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json
import math
import statistics

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
OUT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PRIOR = ROOT / 'target/arm64-recognition-sme-final-20261017'
sha = lambda p: hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
comparison = json.loads((PRIOR / 'page-comparison.json').read_text())
profiles = json.loads((PRIOR / 'profiles.json').read_text())
operators = json.loads((OUT / 'operators.json').read_text())
manifest = json.loads((ROOT / 'tests/baseline/manifest.json').read_text())
labels = {'imgs_1': 'sparse', 'imgs_00018069': 'dense', 'imgs_00006737': 'mixed'}
keys = ['det_preprocess_ns','det_inference_ns','det_postprocess_ns','crop_ns',
        'classification_wall_ns','recognition_wall_ns','total_ns']

def compare_golden(expected, actual):
    for key in ['id','text','detected_count','detector_resized_width','detector_resized_height']:
        assert expected[key] == actual[key], key
    assert len(expected['lines']) == len(actual['lines'])
    for e, a in zip(expected['lines'], actual['lines']):
        for key in ['text','classification_label','applied_rotation_degrees','emitted_count',
                    'recognition_content_width','recognition_tensor_width','recognition_time_steps']:
            assert e[key] == a[key], key
        for key in ['detection_score','recognition_score','classification_score']:
            assert math.isfinite(a[key]) and abs(e[key]-a[key]) <= 1e-4+1e-4*abs(e[key]), key
        assert len(e['points']) == len(a['points'])
        for ep, ap in zip(e['points'],a['points']):
            assert len(ep) == len(ap)
            assert all(math.isfinite(y) and abs(x-y) <= 0.5 for x,y in zip(ep,ap))

cases = []
latency = ['| Bundle / page | Lines | Median ms | Min–max ms | Load ms | First call ms | Peak RSS MiB |',
           '| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |']
stages = ['| Bundle / page | DET prepare | DET infer | DB boxes | Crop | CLS | REC | Total |',
          '| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |']
owners_table = ['| Bundle / page | Width cost range | Owner finish range ms | Longest crop owner finish ms | Last owner maximum crop width |',
                '| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |']
memory = ['| Bundle / page | Retained activations MiB | Retained workspace MiB |', '| --- | ---: | ---: |']
for row in comparison['cases']:
    model, fixture = row['model'], row['fixture']
    a = row['after']
    p = next(p for p in profiles['profiles'] if (p['model'],p['fixture']) == (model,fixture))
    assert p['complete_owned_outputs_exactly_equal']
    assert row['complete_projected_results_exactly_equal']
    assert a['result'] == row['before']['result']
    assert sha(Path(row['job']['pixels'])) == row['job']['pixel_sha256']
    golden = json.loads((ROOT / f'tests/baseline/expected/{model}.json').read_text())
    compare_golden(next(c for c in golden['cases'] if c['id'] == fixture),a['result'])
    s=p['profile']
    remainder=s['total_ns']-sum(s[k] for k in keys[:-1])
    assert remainder >= 0
    cases.append(dict(model=model,fixture=fixture,page=labels[fixture],job=row['job'],measurement=a,
        profile=p,golden_comparison_passed=True,profile_wall_remainder_ns=remainder,
        profile_stage_shares_percent={k:100*s[k]/s['total_ns'] for k in keys[:-1]}))
    title=f'{model.title()} / {labels[fixture]}'
    samples=a['samples_ms']
    latency.append(f'| {title} | {len(a["result"]["lines"])} | {statistics.median(samples):.2f} | {min(samples):.2f}–{max(samples):.2f} | {a["load_compile_ms"]:.2f} | {a["first_inference_ms"]:.2f} | {a["peak_resident_bytes"]/1048576:.2f} |')
    stages.append('| '+title+' | '+' | '.join(f'{s[k]/1e6:.2f}' for k in keys)+' |')
    if fixture != 'imgs_1':
        owners=s['recognition_owners'][:s['recognition_owner_count']]
        ends=[o['dispatch_end_offset_ns']/1e6 for o in owners]
        costs=[o['scheduled_width_cost'] for o in owners]
        long=max(owners,key=lambda o:o['maximum_tensor_width'])
        last=max(owners,key=lambda o:o['dispatch_end_offset_ns'])
        owners_table.append(f'| {title} | {min(costs)}–{max(costs)} | {min(ends):.2f}–{max(ends):.2f} | '+(f'{long["dispatch_end_offset_ns"]/1e6:.2f}' if fixture=='imgs_00006737' else '—')+f' | {last["maximum_tensor_width"]} |')
    if fixture=='imgs_00006737':
        memory.append(f'| {title} | {p["retained_activation_bytes"]["total"]/1048576:.2f} | {p["retained_workspace_bytes"]/1048576:.2f} |')

workkeys=[('Crop workers','crop_work_ns'),('CLS resize and normalize','cls_preprocess_ns'),
          ('CLS backbone','cls_backbone_ns'),('CLS compact head','cls_head_ns'),('CLS pixel rotation','cls_rotation_ns'),
          ('REC resize and normalize','rec_preprocess_ns'),('REC backbone','rec_backbone_ns'),
          ('Vocabulary projection and argmax','projection_ns'),('CTC decode','ctc_ns'),
          ('DET and REC reshape','reshape_ns'),('Binding and validation','binding_ns'),('Result storage','result_storage_ns')]
dense=[c for c in cases if c['page']=='dense']
work=['| Nested worker work ms | Tiny dense | Small dense | Medium dense |','| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |']
for label,k in workkeys:
    work.append('| '+label+' | '+' | '.join(f'{c["profile"]["profile"][k]/1e6:.4f}' for c in dense)+' |')
oprows=['| Fused operator probe | All steps ms | 1×1 convolution ms | 1×1 share | Layout conversion ms |',
        '| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |']
for d in operators['diagnostics']:
    kind='DET sparse, 8 threads' if d['kind']=='detector' else f'REC width {d["shape"][3]}, 1 thread'
    one=d['groups_ms']['Conv 1x1 groups=1']
    oprows.append(f'| {d["model"].title()} {kind} | {d["total_step_ms"]:.3f} | {one:.3f} | {100*one/d["total_step_ms"]:.1f}% | {d["groups_ms"].get("Convert",0):.4f} |')

text=f'''# Current Apple M4 OCR pipeline latency and optimization analysis

At revision `{operators['head']}`, detection remains the main cost on sparse pages, while recognition dominates dense pages. Detector inference accounts for **68.2–77.2%** of sparse-page wall time. Recognition accounts for **58.6%, 79.0% and 85.4%** of dense Tiny, Small and Medium wall time. **The next useful work is convolution execution and recognition scheduling; DB geometry, CTC decoding and result copying have small absolute ceilings on these inputs.** Tiny dense orientation is a separate substantial target at **26.5%** of its profile.

This analysis covers the current SME implementation, including its fallbacks. It supersedes the bottleneck ranking in the [pre-SME pipeline analysis](macos-current-pipeline-analysis.md); the [SME optimization report](macos-arm64-sme-optimization.md) retains the paired before/after speedup evidence. The [complete evidence](reports/{name}) contains current-source hashes, all page samples, nested profiles, owner records, fresh operator timings, validation logs and reproduction scripts.

The page samples were already measured locally on 17 October 2026. Every `src/**/*.rs` hash matches the current checkout exactly; benchmark examples, harness and build configuration are unchanged from their recorded base. Frozen benchmark/profile executable hashes also match. Those samples are retained without rerunning unchanged code. Five new operator probes answer the outstanding question of which network operations dominate after SME. No samples from the pre-SME revision or rejected prototypes are pooled with the current results.

The physical machine is Apple M4, 10 cores, 16 GiB RAM, macOS 27.0.1. Builds use native release, pinned `nightly-2026-09-08`, default parallel features, automatic NEON/FMA with guarded SME, automatic layouts and fusion. Page measurements use eight shared workers, one request, automatic line ownership, adaptive recognition widths, batch one, detector limit 960, classification enabled and alignment disabled. Scheduling is unpinned. The host is on AC power, and `pmset` reports no recorded thermal/performance warning; neither core placement nor clock frequency is measured.

The three inputs are sparse `imgs_1` (720×1150), dense `imgs_00018069` (430×267), and mixed-width `imgs_00006737` (896×528). Their detector tensors are 608×960, 416×256 and 896×544. Different bundles can return different line counts and text, so cross-model speed comparisons do not establish equivalent recognition accuracy.

Ordinary latency starts from hash-verified decoded BGR24 and includes complete owned result conversion. Each of nine cases has one separately recorded first call, one warm-up and three measured calls in a fresh process. Load includes import, compilation, CPU-context and initial request creation. OS file caches were not flushed, so load is not disk-cold latency. Peak RSS is the process lifetime resident high-water mark, including setup and shared pages.

{chr(10).join(latency)}

Measured ranges span 0.3–9.0% of their medians, with Tiny dense the widest. Medium sparse/mixed span 4.6%/6.3%. These three samples support broad bottleneck prioritization, not p95/p99 estimates or small-effect significance. First calls need not always be slower than later calls. Every original first/warm/measured result was checked for complete equality within its case.

The library path is borrowed pixels → detector preparation → detector network → DB boxes → perspective crops → orientation and rotation → recognition preparation/backbone/head/CTC → ordered results. File I/O, image decoding, application serialization and engine admission waiting are outside the reported inference latency. These costs must be measured in the consuming application if its end-to-end latency is the target.

The following elapsed stages come from separate profiling-enabled production runs, each with one warm-up and one instrumented call. All values are milliseconds. The six wall phases are sequential; their sum leaves only 0.012–0.016 ms of orchestration in total. They must not be combined with the ordinary medians above to estimate overhead or a stage speedup.

CLS backbone is 92.8–93.4% of its dense worker orientation time. Vocabulary projection is 7.1%, 6.9% and 4.1% of dense backbone-plus-projection work. CTC stays below 0.042 ms summed work, and warm reshape below 0.052 ms across all nine cases. These figures give little reason to prioritize decoder, result-ownership or warm shape-cache rewrites. Dense profiles apply no 180-degree rotations, while sparse profiles rotate all 3/2/2 lines and mixed profiles rotate 1/2/3; the dense fixture alone does not justify removing classification.

**Small REC:** the 192→384 layers over 192 spatial rows take 0.401–0.421 ms each; the reverse 384→192 layers take about 0.290–0.293 ms. Neither direction passes the current SME channel threshold. Existing SME-eligible 384→768 layers over 96 rows still take 0.421–0.427 ms. A useful next experiment is the exact 192-row, K=192, N=384 shape, including input packing and fused stores, to establish whether a lower crossover or a better NEON kernel helps.

**Medium REC:** repeated 512→1024 layers over 960 rows take 6.67–6.94 ms, while 768→1536 layers take 5.89–6.02 ms. These are already SME-eligible. Below-threshold 256→512 layers over 1920 rows take 5.84–5.87 ms, with reverse layers around 4.45–4.50 ms. Both improving retained SME execution and testing the narrower crossover have concrete targets. Attention MatMul, softmax, layer normalization and transpose together account for only 1.3%/1.2% of Small/Medium probe time.

Recognition owner completion provides another optimization lead. Width cost is the sum of scheduled recognition tensor widths; finish offsets share one dispatch origin. All listed owners begin within 0.5 ms. Dense owners use one kernel thread each. Mixed pages give only the longest single-crop owner two threads.

{chr(10).join(owners_table)}

For Medium dense, width costs differ by only 9.7%, but completion ranges from 239.64 to 484.46 ms. The slowest owner uses 484.01 ms of calling-thread CPU during its 484.45 ms wall interval. Medium mixed's 1472-wide crop finishes at 411.51 ms, **68.08 ms before** the last owner, whose maximum crop width is 480. Tiny and Small's longest crops also finish before their last owners. Further special-casing only the longest crop therefore misses the observed critical path.

These observations support investigating owner cost estimation, available parallel work and SME execution under concurrent owners. They do not prove a P/E-core placement issue, memory-bandwidth bottleneck or SME hardware contention. Thread CPU clocks exclude helpers and do not distinguish useful arithmetic from active stalls. A next scheduling probe should record per-owner kernel selection and hardware placement if available, then test a deterministic policy with bounded memory. Blind work stealing would risk the stable ownership and buffer-reuse properties that the current code intentionally preserves.

{chr(10).join(memory)}

Medium mixed additionally peaks at 480.78 MiB RSS. Retained activation/workspace sizes and RSS measure different things; immutable model/packed weights, allocator behavior and shared pages also contribute. More simultaneous requests can multiply private scratch, so a latency gain needs memory validation.

The practical priority depends on the workload:

1. **Small/Medium dense or mixed pages:** optimize pointwise convolutions and diagnose the Medium owner imbalance. Test one exact below-threshold shape and one already-SME shape before changing dispatch broadly. Preserve reduction order, bias, tails, fused epilogues and fallback behavior.
2. **Sparse pages:** optimize detector convolution, especially measured smaller-channel pointwise and 3×3 layers. The recent SME work did not remove detector dominance.
3. **Tiny dense pages:** target orientation backbone or classifier batching alongside recognition. Removing CLS is an application option only with an upright-input contract and output checks; it changes behavior on the rotated sparse/mixed inputs.
4. **Secondary work:** detector resize/normalization, compact vocabulary projection, and verified exact-width REC batching. Batch support already exists; it is not automatically faster and can reduce independent work. Smaller models or detector resolutions require a separate ground-truth accuracy/latency tradeoff study.
5. **Defer for these inputs:** DB geometry, CTC, result copying and more warm shape caching. Their measured costs cannot explain the main latency.

For scale, a hypothetical **20% reduction of the whole REC phase** saves **7.64/25.61/96.90 ms** on dense Tiny/Small/Medium, or **11.7%/15.8%/17.1%** of profiled page time. Halving Tiny dense CLS saves **8.62 ms (13.2%)**. A 20% DET inference reduction saves **14.1%/13.6%/15.4%** of sparse Tiny/Small/Medium time. These are sensitivity calculations with other stages fixed, not measured candidate speedups; kernel-only improvements have smaller page effects.
